Subject: Your next trip just got a reliable light source: meet the Beacon
Preview: 400 lumens. 40 hours. 95 grams. USB-C. That's the whole pitch.
Body: Whether you're on day three of a backpacking trip or setting up camp after a long drive in, you need a headlamp that's already charged and ready to work through the night.

The Northbay Beacon is built around three numbers:

• 400 lumens — enough to navigate trail, read a map, or cook a real meal in the dark
• 40 hours of runtime — so a single charge covers a multi-day trip on lower modes without rationing
• 95 grams — light enough that you'll forget it's on your head

It charges over USB-C, which means one cable for your phone, your battery bank, and your headlamp. No proprietary chargers to hunt down before a trip.

A honest note: the Beacon is a trail and camp headlamp. It's not designed for technical caving or commercial dive lighting — if that's your use case, you'll want a more specialized tool.

For most three-season backcountry use, it will do the job without asking for much in return.
Score 0-1; a score below 0.75 is a fail.
